title: Enabling high-accuracy lithium-ion battery status prediction via machine learning-integrated perovskite sensors
Physics-informed weakly supervised learning for in-situ photoluminescence dynamics analysis in perovskite solar cells
abstract: Crystallization of perovskites is the key process in thin film perovskite solar cells (PSCs). The ability to connect film formation dynamics with device performance remains a central challenge in the development of high-performance PSCs. Here, we develop a deep spatiotemporal attention network that outputs a current density-voltage (J-V) curve for each in-situ photoluminescence (PL) patch. Training follows a weak-supervision paradigm: only the global J-V is observed, and learning is driven by aligning the aggregation of local predictions with this global target. Visual Explanation analysis via gradient-based activation map (GAM) indicates that the model focuses on physically meaningful stages of film evolution—capturing early nucleation dynamics and later crystallization—while emphasizing longer-wavelength PL signals during late stages and shorter-wavelength cues during nucleation. Beyond global prediction, the local J-V outputs enable spatial diagnostics: using Spearman’s rank correlation, we find a statistically significant negative monotonic association between the dispersion of local power conversion efficiency (PCE) and overall PCE, which strengthens on well-estimated samples. Together, these results suggest that spatially uniform local performance is a strong indicator of high-performance device and highlight PL-video-driven deep learning as a scalable data-driven workflow for both performance prediction and process optimization in industry. To demonstrate industrial applicability of solar cells, this AI model integrates into scalable production lines like blade-coating. By rapidly evaluating uniformity and predicting performance, it enables a real-time feedback loop for immediate process adjustments, ensuring consistent, high-quality manufacturing. • A model based on Transformer architecture and weak supervision is developed to enable the rapid and precise prediction of the local performance of a perovskite film. • The results demonstrate a marked improvement in predictive capability: The prediction accuracy improves from 0.472 to 0.504. The prediction error is substantially reduced, with the Mean Absolute Error decreasing from 1.488 to 1.358. • A clear negative correlation emerges: devices with lower global Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) tend to exhibit higher spatial variability in the predicted local efficiencies, whereas devices with higher global PCEs display more uniform local predictions.

title: Dominance of the carbon–oxygen framework over dopants in hydrogen peroxide electrosynthesis on metal-free carbons
abstract: Heteroatom-doped metal-free carbon catalysts (HMCs) achieve high selectivity for the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e⁻ ORR) to hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), yet mechanism assignments remain disputed. We identify three recurrent sources of disagreement: assuming dopant-centered active sites while the carbon–oxygen framework co-evolves; small, single-study sample sets amplified by within-element ratios; and inconsistent electrochemical and XPS reporting. To resolve this, we establish a cross-study evidence standard combining standardized electrochemical metrics, survey-anchored absolute atomic quantification, and DOI-grouped validation. Across alkaline studies, performance clusters in a narrow region of high sp 2 connectivity and moderate oxygenation ( sp ² fraction ≈82–88% and O ≈8–15 at%), associated with ≥ 90% H 2 O 2 selectivity and favorable onsets. In an exclusive N-doped subset, nitrogen descriptors do not generalize under the same criteria. Machine learning-guided density functional theory on controlled sp ²/ sp ³ frameworks with and without substitutional N corroborates the framework-first mechanism: the sp ²/ sp ³ ratio (balance) governs *OOH thermodynamics, whereas N produces only minor changes. Demonstrated here for alkaline 2e - ORR on HMCs, the evidence standard is transferable to other mechanistically disputed catalytic systems.

title: PhyTENG: A physics-informed machine learning framework for modelling contact - separation triboelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising for harvesting mechanical energy and enabling self-powered sensing. Their electrical performance depends on complex interactions among materials, device architecture, and operating conditions and it is challenging to make accurate prediction models. In this work, we present PhyTENG, a physics-informed machine learning (ML) framework to predict output voltage and current in contact-separation (CS) TENGs. A diverse experimental dataset was curated from literature and augmented with open-source materials databases and ML-based property predictors to obtain atomic- and surface-level physics-based descriptors, including electron affinity, ionisation energy, and triboelectric charge density. Four interpretable gradient-boosting models were then trained to relate these properties and other descriptors to their electrical performance. We further demonstrate the advantages of using physics-inspired descriptors relative to conventional categorical materials featurisation. Overall, the presented PhyTENG framework provides a generalisable predictive tool for TENG optimisation and a pathway to integrate AI-driven materials discovery with AI-driven device design.

title: 2D thermal imaging of large-format batteries using distributed optical fiber sensing and physics-informed neural networks
Machine learning-aided high-temperature polymer composites for capacitive energy storage
Unraveling the design rules for enhancing stability of organic photovoltaic materials under accelerated aging conditions through machine learning
Unified multitask decoding and interaction enabled by physics-informed spatial information enhancement framework
Light polarization as a control knob for resistive switching in chiral perovskite memory
abstract: Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based on metal-halide perovskites has attracted significant interest for neuromorphic and in-memory computing applications owing to its simple structure and tunable material properties. However, practical implementation is limited by stochastic filament formation and the lack of effective control parameters beyond electrical bias and light intensity. Here, we introduce light polarization as an independent control variable for resistive switching using a chiral perovskite RRAM device. Owing to the intrinsic circular dichroism of the chiral perovskite, right- and left-circularly polarized light (RCP and LCP) generate different photocarrier populations under identical illumination intensity, enabling deterministic modulation of switching behavior. As a result, the set voltage (Vset) is reduced from 0.15 V in the dark to 0.10 V and 0.05 V under RCP and LCP, respectively, accompanied by improved switching uniformity. Conduction mechanism analysis reveals that polarization-dependent photocarrier generation induces a transition from interface-limited to bulk-dominated transport, thereby stabilizing filament nucleation. In addition, the incorporation of bulky chiral ligands, which enhances chirality, leads to enlarged interlayer spacing that facilitates uniform Ag ion infiltration and suppresses stochastic filament formation. Finally, polarization-modulated synaptic characteristics are demonstrated, and artificial neural network simulations show enhanced learning performance. These results demonstrate that polarization-driven control of resistive switching can be effectively reinforced by structural engineering, establish light polarization as a new control knob for resistive switching, and provide a viable pathway toward multifunctional memory and neuromorphic applications.

title: Machine learning-guided design of rare-earth single-atom catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction
Machine learning-based force and activity recognition in total knee replacement using hybrid triboelectric/piezoelectric PVDF sensors
abstract: Smart orthopedic implants require sensing systems that can monitor joint loading without increasing dependence on batteries or complex implanted electronics. Here, we report an implant-integrated hybrid triboelectric-piezoelectric nanogenerator (TPNG) built from six multilayer Cu/PVDF transducers distributed across the medial and lateral compartments of a tibial-tray-inspired total knee replacement (TKR) package. Coupling triboelectric contact-separation to the piezoelectric response of the stack increases the peak-to-peak voltage, while the transducers retain 92.4% of their peak-to-peak output after approximately 350,000 gait cycles. The present study evaluates the sensors under predominantly centered axial loading, which consists of 90% of loading going through the knee joint. Using a single full-wave rectifier across all six transducers charges a 0.22 μ F capacitor to 68.1 V, corresponding to 509.9 μ J of stored energy, and drives a 168-LED array, demonstrating practical energy delivery from physiological joint loading. In addition, the machine learning algorithms are integrated for force and activity recognition. Using five independent 120-cycle recordings per activity with recording-level data separation, the CNN-BiLSTM classifier achieved 99.7% accuracy on the held-out recording across eight activities. A separate CNN-BiLSTM model further provided proof-of-concept reconstruction of an unseen patient's axial force profile from PVDF voltage alone. Together, these results establish a multifunctional PVDF-based sensing architecture that combines energy harvesting, fatigue-resistant transduction, and learned biomechanical interpretation from a single device, providing a pathway toward battery-free smart joint implants.

title: Energy-efficient, high-accuracy sensing in loose-fitting textile sensor matrix for LLM-enabled human-robot collaboration
abstract: Textile-based sensing systems hold significant promise for wearable human–robot interfaces, but many existing approaches lack one or more key attributes, such as pixel-level self-powering, high spatial resolution, or the ability to balance wearing comfort with sensing accuracy and reliability. Furthermore, few solutions demonstrate adaptability across physical platforms or integration with semantic reasoning frameworks. Here, we present a multifunctional textile sensor matrix (TSM) that addresses these limitations by combining woven Schottky-diode junctions for localized self-powered sensing, deep learning (DL) for denoising and feature extraction, and large language model (LLM) integration for high-level task planning. Each pixel, approximately 300 µm × 400 µm in size, provides dual-mode output for pressure sensing and energy harvesting, achieving 75 mV kPa−1 voltage sensitivity, 0.82 nA kPa−1 current sensitivity, and 14 µW cm−2 power output. Each sensing pixel measures ∼300 µm × 400 µm, with an achieved density of ∼48 cm−2. The system achieves 98.22 % accuracy in gesture recognition, 97.02 % in object identification, and 94.03 % in robotic hand adaptation via transfer learning. Beyond perception, integration with LLM supports high-level task planning, establishing a tactile-language-action (TLA) framework. This work introduces a scalable, energy-efficient, and cognitively integrated textile platform for adaptive human–robot collaboration and embodied AI.

title: Self-powered heart real-time monitoring system based on triboelectric and piezoelectric hybrid nanogenerator and artificial intelligence technology
abstract: By converting biomechanical energy from human walking into electrical energy, the triboelectric and piezoelectric hybrid nanogenerator (TPHG) can immediately and sustainably power the heart rate monitoring system. The designed system displays a swift runtime of 14 ms and low energy consumption at 220 μJ. The acquired electrocardiogram (ECG) signals can be transferred by a wireless module to an artificial intelligence (AI) cloud server and displayed on a smartphone or personal computer in real time. This work paves the key way for designing self-powered real-time monitoring systems.

title: Spatiotemporal decoding of laryngeal motion using flexible triboelectric arrays and deep learning assistance
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has driven innovations in human-machine interaction through tightly coupled perception systems. Electronic skins (e-skins) are a crucial technology for developing these perceptive capabilities. However, existing e-skins face challenges such as reliance on external power, complex fabrication, and signal processing sophistication. Here, we introduce a screen-printed triboelectric sensor array (TSA) integrated with a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) for high-fidelity laryngeal motion decoding, to establish an intelligent laryngeal muscle decoding system. The conductive silver paste with exceptional electrical conductivity (0.23 Ω/sq) function as electrode in the TSA, enabling high sensitivity (1.651 V/kPa), good mechanical durability and seamless epidermal integration. By harnessing the 2D-CNN's spatiotemporal feature extraction capability, the system achieves 99.6 % accuracy in classifying laryngeal movements, surpassing conventional time-series analysis methods. The proposed system enables concurrent high-spatial-resolution tactile sensing, and pressure sensing, demonstrating remarkable superiority over human tactile acuity in both resolution and sensitivity. This study presents a self-powered, flexible sensing system capable of decoding subtle laryngeal muscle motions. By integrating a deep learning model, the system effectively classifies laryngeal motion patterns associated with specific words, offering a new possibility for the exploration of speech rehabilitation and next-generation wearable human-computer interaction.

title: Advances in machine learning (ML)-driven design of two-dimensional materials for energy and environmental applications
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials, with atomic-scale thickness, tunable electronic structures, and complex interfacial chemistry, are attracting increasing attention for sustainable energy conversion and environmental remediation. However, conventional experimental and first-principles screening methods remain slow and costly, restricting exploration of their vast compositional and structural diversity. This review summarizes recent progress in machine learning (ML)-assisted design of 2D materials, highlighting commonly applied supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised algorithms, feature-engineering techniques, and open databases. The integration of ML with density functional theory (DFT) accelerates the discovery of high-performance electrodes, guides the optimization of electrocatalysts and photocatalysts, and enables efficient screening of thermoelectric, sensing, desalination, and pollutant-removal systems. Emerging ML applications in toxicity evaluation and safety assessment are also discussed. Key challenges in data quality, descriptor construction, model generalization, and physical interpretability are analyzed, while future directions in physics-guided learning, automated ML, and multi-objective optimization are outlined. Overall, this review offers a comprehensive perspective that links machine learning with the rational design of 2D materials for sustainable energy and environmental systems.

title: Physics-guided machine learning for co-design of charge-pumped triboelectric nanogenerators at critical air-breakdown
abstract: Operating charge-pumped triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) at the critical air-breakdown state is essential for maximizing power output, yet it intensifies the fundamental trade-off with durability, creating a complex co-design challenge. Herein, this study first systematically investigates electromechanical mechanism in charge-pumped rotary freestanding TENG (RF-TENG) at the critical air-breakdown state. Experiments reveal that the dynamic evolution of the transfer film governs the competition between the output charge density and the wear loss, enabling establishment of the quantitative relationships among wear loss, transfer film coverage ratio and output charge density. Then, leveraging this insight, an electromechanical model is established and further a physics-guided hybrid surrogate model is constructed through integration of conditioned-modulation Gaussian process regression (CMGPR) and artificial neural network (ANN). The CMGPR-ANN framework provides efficient performance evaluation, where CMGPR enables stage-aware wear prediction while ANN captures nonlinear electrostatic induction. Ultimately, by combining this hybrid model with multi-objective optimization, the Pareto frontier between electrical performance and durability is mapped, extracting quantitative design principles for key parameters (e.g., the gap ratio) and delivering optimal designs for high-performance charge-pumped RF-TENG. This work establishes a co-design paradigm bridging physical mechanisms with computational optimization for advanced TENG development.

title: Gradient-architected magnetic tactile skin for human-vehicle interaction: From bio-inspired design to deep learning-enabled recognition of driver operational behaviors
abstract: In the foreseeable future, human drivers will remain an indispensable role of autonomous vehicles, rendering real-time and accurate recognition of driver operational behaviors critical for driving safety and cooperative decision-making. Although flexible tactile sensors offer a promising solution for capturing driver-vehicle interactions, driver operational behaviors span a wide range of interaction forces, from subtle pre-operational cues to large-amplitude control actions, posing a significant challenge for conventional tactile sensors to achieve both high sensitivity and a broad sensing range. Inspired by the hierarchical mechanosensing mechanism of human skin, this study proposes a biomimetic gradient-structured flexible magnetic skin (BG-FMS) for fine-grained driver operational behavior recognition. The designed three-gradient elastic modulus architecture enables the BG-FMS to simultaneously provide high sensitivity to subtle operational cues and a wide dynamic range for large-amplitude driving actions, while maintaining fast response and strong environmental robustness. The BG-FMS is seamlessly integrated on the steering wheel and pedal surfaces, enabling real-time acquisition of driver operational signals. Meanwhile, a channel attention-enhanced deep learning model (CA-TCNet) is developed to accurately recognize driver operational behaviors. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed driver operational behavior recognition system achieves recognition accuracies of 99.6%, 98.0%, and 90.7% using 3 s, 2 s, and 1 s of operation data, respectively, highlighting its ultra-fast early-stage behavior recognition capability. This work presents a robust, non-intrusive, and deployable human-vehicle interaction sensing solution, thereby broadening the application scope of flexible magnetic skins in intelligent transportation and cooperative driving systems.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven paradigms for layered cathode materials: A systematic framework for multi-scale engineering
abstract: Layered cathode materials, exemplified by lithium/sodium-based layered oxides, stand at the forefront of battery research owing to their high energy density and superior ion transport characteristics. However, their design and performance optimization encounter multiscale challenges. At the atomic scale, issues include cation mixing and the unregulated oxygen redox behaviors; at the crystal scale, phase transitions and stress distributions pose significant hurdles; while at the particle scale, crack evolution and interfacial stability remain critical concerns. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are inefficient, particularly when addressing the complex interscale couplings inherent in these systems.The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced a transformative paradigm in materials design. By synergistically integrating data-driven methodologies with fundamental physical models, AI enables cross-scale optimization—ranging from atomic defect engineering to macroscopic performance prediction. AI applications in high-throughput screening, crystal structure prediction, and dynamic process analysis have markedly accelerated the discovery and development of advanced materials. Nevertheless, critical challenges persist, including ensuring data quality and representativeness, enhancing model interpretability, and bridging the gap between computational predictions and experimental validation. This review establishes a systematic framework for evaluating AI-driven paradigms in the context of layered cathode materials, providing a multi-scale perspective that spans from atomic-level discovery to electrode-level optimization, thereby highlighting the innovative potential of AI to overcome performance bottlenecks and drive the advancement of next-generation battery technologies.

title: Bifunctional organohydrogel-based self-powered omnidirectional pressure-sensing smart ball with deep learning assistance for comprehensive hand rehabilitation assessment
abstract: Hand function rehabilitation is essential for restoring motor ability, but remains challenging due to complex biomechanics of hand, and limited omnidirectional sensing capability of existing self-powered portable devices. To overcome these challenges, we present PEDOT:PSS-doped bifunctional organohydrogel (PPBOH) based self-powered pressure-sensing stress ball (SPSB) designed for comprehensive, direction-independent monitoring of complex hand exercises. Incorporating large semiconducting polymer PEDOT: PSS into organohydrogel significantly enhanced its tribopositivity, electrical conductivity, and mechanical robustness while maintaining compressibility, resulting in two-fold increase in output voltage (621 V), and power density (1.7 W/m2). Leveraging intrinsic shape adaptability of PPBOH and facile molding approach, conical arrays were molded on PPBOH sphere, encapsulated in electronegative silicone shell, and shielded with outer PPBOH layer that effectively suppresses skin-induced triboelectric interference. The resulting SPSB exhibits superior omnidirectional sensitivity (0.453 V/N, 2.8–40 N; 0.069 V/N, 40–90 N), stability (21k cycles), mechanical compliance, and reproducibility (±6%). The SPSB was successfully employed for real-time monitoring of comprehensive hand-rehabilitation exercises and trained with deep learning model to effectively identify exercise patterns with excellent accuracy (98%). Moreover, grip strength was evaluated using s-EMG signals as reference metric that directly maps voltage and force through customized interactive rehabilitation platform. Collectively, a portable, omnidirectional pressure-sensing ball has been developed, marking substantial advance toward continuous, home-based neuromuscular rehabilitation monitoring.

title: Artificial intelligence–enabled design of a four-bar linkage triboelectric nanogenerator for wave energy harvesting
abstract: Power take-off (PTO) mechanisms are key devices that convert ocean wave energy into mechanical energy for triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs)-based wave energy converter. However, conventional PTO mechanisms, including gears and screws, are structurally complex, require high assembly precision, and are difficult to maintain, which limits their potential for large‑scale engineering applications. Moreover, the PTO mechanism parameter optimization typically depends on numerous single-variable experiments, leading to high costs and limiting the potential for globally optimal designs. Here, we propose a novel wave energy converter (WEC) whose core is a planar four‑bar linkage that converts the heaving motion of a wave‑driven buoy into the reciprocating rotation of a main shaft, and then drives the TENG rotor into unidirectional rotation via one‑way bearings for continuous electricity generation. This design not only simplifies the PTO structure but also enhances energy harvesting efficiency during both upward and downward motions. We establish a kinematic model of the PTO mechanism to predict the angular velocity of the TENG rotor, and verify the model through theoretical calculation and experimental testing of the short‑circuit current of the TENG unit. Next, we propose an AI‑assisted mechanism optimization method that uses the kinematic model to generate a dataset, combined with artificial neural network training and intelligent algorithm search, with the TENG rotor kinetic energy as the optimization objective, to optimize the mechanism parameters. This enables PTO parameters to be tailored for specific marine environments without extensive physical testing. The optimized device achieves peak and average power densities of 3.83 W/m3 and 0.746 W/m3, respectively, and after power management demonstrates the ability to power small electronic devices. This work provides a timely and cost-effective strategy for optimizing PTO mechanisms in TENG-based WECs, accelerating the transition from laboratory research to practical applications.

title: Artificial intelligence assisted self-powered water quality monitoring and early warning using a triboelectric-electromagnetic hybrid generator
abstract: Water pollution warning serves as a critical first line of defense in safeguarding public health and preserving aquatic ecosystems, especially amid growing industrial and urban pressures. However, the implementation of real-time, distributed monitoring systems along extensive pipeline networks remains hindered by formidable obstacles, including unreliable power access and limitations in real-time data analysis and predictive capacity. To address these issues, we propose a water quality sensing triboelectric and electromagnetic hybrid generator (WQS-TEHG). Via synergistic biomimetic fish-fin blade optimization and a storage-release electromagnetic generator (SR-EMG), the system harvests energy efficiently across a wide flow-velocity range. An optimized triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) sensing unit integrated with a total dissolved solids (TDS) sensor forms a multi-parameter sensing suite, its flow-sensing output frequency shows a strong linear correlation with actual flow velocity (Coefficient of determination (R²) ≈ 0.96). Building on this hardware, we develop a Temporal-Spatial convolutional network (TSCN) for early warning. By integrating spatiotemporal features from flow and TDS, the model enables the early detection of water-quality issues and delivers highly accurate parameter predictions, substantially outperforming single-input baselines (R² +0.08, RMSE −11.8). This work addresses energy constraints and limited intelligence in urban pipeline monitoring and lays the groundwork for distributed self-powered, intelligent water-monitoring networks.

title: Artificial intelligence -driven triboelectric nanogenerators for healthcare: Devices, algorithms and systems
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) can convert biomechanical and biochemical stimuli into electrical signals without an external power source, thus enabling wearable and implantable health monitoring systems. However, triboelectric signals are sparse, nonstationary, and highly sensitive to motion, humidity, contact changes, and device aging. Their clinical value therefore depends not only on device sensitivity, but also on algorithms that transform unstable self-powered waveforms into reliable physiological information. This article reviews the intelligent TENG health-monitoring system from the perspective of the collaborative design of devices and algorithms. We first survey self-powered sensors for sweat and body-fluid analysis, pulse and blood-pressure monitoring, respiration, ocular and facial-muscle motion, implantable cardiac monitoring, and self-powered pacing. We then trace the algorithmic evolution from hand-crafted-feature machine learning to convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, multimodal, and neuromorphic models, linking each model family to the signal bottleneck it addresses. We argue that in the next stage of TENG health monitoring will no longer mainly be defined by peak output or isolated recognition accuracy, but will more reflect aspects such as calibration stability, cross-subject generalization, motion artifact suppression, energy efficiency, and clinical interpretability. Emerging architectures like state-space models and reservoir computing may provide the computational basis for low-power, real-time health systems.

title: Concurrent self-powered static-force-sensing and power-supplying triboelectric nanogenerator via electron avalanche and machine learning
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence and internet of things sensors, global energy consumption has become a major challenge. Many researchers have aimed to develop self-powered sensors based on energy harvesting; however, these devices still generate a low-power output, which is insufficient to power an entire system. Among the various energy-harvesting technologies, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising candidates that can be easily applied to self-powered sensors. Nevertheless, TENGs have a critical limitation; although they can generate a high-voltage output, the fundamental generation mechanism inherently limits the current output to low levels. In this study, a self-powered, static-force-sensing TENG capable of functioning concurrently as a self-powered sensor and power supplier was demonstrated. Through the electrostatic discharge effect, this system generated a high electrical output via an electron avalanche during air breakdown and regulated the voltage signal through the gap distance according to Paschen's law. Consequently, this system achieved high sensing accuracy using a random forest regression model and exhibited energy-harvesting capability by powering 3000 LEDs and seven 5-W lamps and continuously operating three thermo-hygrometers.

title: TENG-based self-powered knee joint motion decoding and AI-assisted evaluation system
abstract: The growing prevalence of knee degenerative diseases has increased the demand for lightweight, continuous, and quantitative monitoring technologies for home-based functional assessment. Herein, a sliding freestanding-layer knee-motion triboelectric nanogenerator (KM-TENG) is developed for self-powered knee motion decoding and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted functional evaluation. A 3D-printed elastic traction structure converts rotational knee motion into controllable linear sliding. By integrating a biomass composite triboelectric layer and interdigital-block coupled electrodes, the KM-TENG achieves stable electrical output and displacement encoding. Cyclic tests verify excellent long-term stability, and continuous knee angle decoding is achieved with an angular resolution of approximately 4.77°. After optical flow calibration and time delay correction, the decoded angular trajectories show high consistency with references. Combined with mechanical modeling and commercial force gauge calibration, leave-one-subject-out cross-validation yields a mean absolute error of 3.56 N and a mean percentage error of only 0.96%. Based on multi-dimensional kinematic, mechanical, and triboelectric features, the AI-assisted module realizes interpretable feedback for motion quality evaluation, load risk warning, and rehabilitation guidance. This passive, lightweight, and low-cost wearable scheme provides reliable technical support for early screening of knee degeneration and home-based rehabilitation assessment.

title: AI-enabled flexible sensing technologies for safety engineering: Materials, devices, and applications
abstract: Safety engineering underpins the resilience and stability of modern industrial and societal infrastructures; however, conventional rigid monitoring systems remain constrained by limited conformability, adaptability and real-time responsiveness in complex and dynamic environments. The convergence of flexible electronics and artificial intelligence (AI) offers a transformative route from passive signal acquisition to active cognitive decision-making. Here, we provide a systematic overview of AI-enabled flexible sensing systems for critical safety applications. We first categorize functional materials by dimensionality and discuss material design strategies that enable mechanical compliance, environmental robustness and sensing capability. Building upon this materials foundation, we further examine computational architectures that transform multimodal sensing signals into actionable intelligence, with emphasis on deep learning-based diagnostics, edge computing frameworks, and neuromorphic devices that alleviate centralized processing constraints. We contextualize these advances across representative safety scenarios, including structural health monitoring, occupational risk assessment, power infrastructure inspection, and fire detection. Finally, we discuss the key challenges, including reliability, scalability, and long-term stability, that must be addressed to enable the transition from assisted monitoring toward autonomous and resilient safety systems. By bridging materials innovation and intelligent computation, AI-enabled flexible sensing technologies are positioned to shift safety engineering from reactive protection to predictive and cognitive paradigms.

title: MEMFNet: Toward a knowledge-guided paradigm for interpretable electrochemical performance prediction
abstract: Understanding and predicting the electrochemical behavior of high-nickel cathode materials remains a central challenge in developing advanced lithium-ion energy storage systems. Although recent machine learning methods have achieved remarkable predictive performance, their generic architectures seldom embody the underlying physical and chemical mechanisms governing electrochemical processes, which limits both interpretability and generalization. We present MEMFNet, a deep learning framework specifically designed to reflect materials science knowledge through a dual-pathway architecture that mirrors the distinction between static material properties and dynamic electrochemical processes. Trained on 158,200 voltage-capacity data points from 791 discharge profiles of high-nickel cathode materials, MEMFNet reduces prediction error by 48.64 % compared to state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, the knowledge-guided architecture transforms the model from a black box into an interpretable system whose learned representations align with established electrochemical principles. By integrating domain knowledge, MEMFNet enables interpretable and scientifically meaningful learning in materials informatics.

title: A highly-integrated flexible triboelectric vibration sensing system for intelligent industrial monitoring on curved surfaces
abstract: The secure and stable operation of energy and industrial systems relies heavily on accurate vibration monitoring. However, conventional rigid vibration sensors face challenges in achieving conformal attachment to the curved surfaces ubiquitous in industrial equipment, leading to signal distortion and limiting deployment flexibility. While emerging flexible sensors offer some improvements, they often encounter limitations such as sensitivity to electromagnetic interference, poor low-frequency response, or complex fabrication processes. To address these challenges, this study presents a fully flexible, highly-integrated triboelectric vibration monitoring system centered on a conical microstructure-based flexible triboelectric vibration sensor (CMF-TVS) for intelligent mechanical condition monitoring. At the device level, the CMF-TVS is constructed by coupling a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) nanofiber film with a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer featuring conical microstructures. This point-contact triboelectric interface lowers the mechanical activation threshold and enables stable signal generation under small-amplitude excitation. The CMF-TVS achieves a broadband frequency response of 30–1000 Hz, detects vibration amplitudes as small as 0.127 μm, and maintains stability over 12,000 cycles. Benefiting from the intrinsic flexibility of both the sensing unit and structural design, the system conforms robustly to planar and curved surfaces. Furthermore, the system integrates a hybrid neural network, achieving a remarkable state recognition accuracy of 98.75% for eight different mechanical operating conditions, demonstrating significant potential for self-powered, in-situ vibration monitoring in complex industrial environments. This work provides a readily deployable, flexible solution for achieving long-term and in-situ vibration monitoring in practical complex industrial environments.

title: Dynamic charge-balanced multi-layer noncontact triboelectric nanogenerator sensors with surface spiral micro-structures for intelligent robotic motion following
abstract: The advances in human-robot interaction (HRI) have brought an immense possibility across diverse application domains. The noncontact triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) sensors have been invented as an efficient proximity sensing tool, but the surface charge density decays quickly and the electrical output performance is still inferior, limiting the intelligent usage based on data consistency. Herein, Co-NPC/Ecoflex, MXene/Ecoflex, CCTO/Ecoflex, Carbon Black/Ecoflex stable functional inks were prepared by adding organic solvent isopropanol. Furthermore, an integrated non-contact TENG sensor with high specific surface area charge generation layer, high electronegativity charge trapping layer, high dielectric constant charge blocking layer, and high conductivity charge collection layer was prepared by ink direct writing. Through thorough optimization of material selection, component composition and structure design, the developed sensor with an effective electrode area of 6.25 cm2 delivers a high output voltage of 24 V at 1 mm, capable of detecting motions at an extremely far distance of 5.5 m. The stability of the device can reach 150 h. A single sensor can be used for one-dimensional human-machine motion following. An electronic patch made of 3 × 3 sensor array is arranged and corresponding neural network algorithm is trained to realize the robotic two-dimensional motion following with an accuracy of 97.6%, which shows potential in developing advanced intelligent HRI.

title: Data-driven discovery of highly efficient 2D photocatalytic materials for water splitting
abstract: Efficient discovery of 2D photocatalysts for water splitting is hindered by the high computational cost of accurate electronic structure calculations and the frequent neglect of realistic operational conditions. Here, we address both challenges by combining a machine learning meta-model trained on GW bandgaps (R2 = 0.985, MAE = 0.18 eV) with cost-effective IPA@PBE optical and Mott-Wannier excitonic descriptors to screen over 20,000 2D materials, ultimately identifying six candidates with suitable band alignments, strong solar absorption, and low exciton binding energies. Non-adiabatic molecular dynamics simulations reveal that four Janus candidates (SbSeI, SbTeI, AsSeI, and AsTeI) exhibit ultralong nonradiative recombination lifetimes of 90.50–121.89 ns, arising from remarkably weak electron-phonon coupling. Finite-temperature analysis shows that a 300 K environment enhances solar absorption via a visible red shift, yet thermal bandgap narrowing eliminates PdSe2 from consideration, highlighting the necessity of moving beyond conventional 0 K screening. Constant-potential implicit solvent calculations further demonstrate that candidates such as AsTeI and SbTeI can overcome the thermodynamic bottleneck of the oxygen evolution reaction under weakly acidic to strongly alkaline conditions. This work provides a scalable, physically grounded strategy for photocatalyst discovery under realistic temperature and solid-liquid interface conditions.

title: From bio-composite to intelligent system: A CM-based triboelectric nanogenerator for self-powered smart packaging and fruit recognition
abstract: The damage caused by transportation to fresh agricultural products is a major challenge in the logistics field. The traditional packaging systems are passive and cannot provide real-time monitoring functions. Moreover, the acceleration and pressure sensors currently used for collision monitoring are facing issues such as power dependence, high costs, and environmental problems. Frictional electric nanogenerators (TENGs) can convert mechanical stimuli into electrical signals, providing an innovative approach for achieving self-powered and intelligent food packaging systems, with enhanced functionality, sustainability, and interactivity. Here, we prepared a chitosan-gelatin (Csgel)/CNC/MXene (CM) composite bio-film using cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-bridged MXene hybrid material as the functional filler and Csgel as the matrix. Based on this film, we further constructed a self-powered and environmentally friendly CM-TENG system to monitor the collisions of fruits during transportation packaging. The CM biofilm has broad-spectrum antibacterial properties, with an antibacterial rate of up to 99.99% against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Its antioxidant performance is up to 75.34%, and its UV shielding UPF value is up to 138.08, providing good preservation effects for strawberries. The device's electrical energy conversion efficiency (instantaneous area power density of 5.8 W m−2 and force sensitivity (24.65 V·N⁻¹)) makes CM-TENG a potential sensor for monitoring the collisions of fresh agricultural products in the packaging during logistics. CM-TENG collects mechanical vibrations during fruit transportation and converts them into real-time electrical signals. The simulation measurement of strawberry transportation indicates that the sensor's electrical output increases with the increase in impact force. This can remind drivers to reduce vibration and minimize mechanical damage to the fruits. Additionally, the characteristic electrical signals generated by different fruit impacts combined with convolutional neural networks (CNN) for recognition have an identification accuracy of up to 98.0% for 8 types of fruits. This study demonstrates that CM-TENG can effectively monitor collision damage during fruit transportation and can identify different fruit types, providing new ideas for intelligent food packaging systems.

title: Intelligent droplet-driven multi-electrode system for decoding triboelectric signals toward heavy metal ion identification
abstract: Accurate identification and quantification of heavy-metal ions in wastewater remain challenging due to the coupled influence of ion species and concentration on interfacial charge transfer at the liquid-solid interface. To address this issue, an intelligent droplet-driven multi-electrode system (IDMS) is presented that leverages droplet dynamics and charge transfer at the liquid-solid interface to generate multi-channel triboelectric signals with clear temporal and spatial relationships. Its response varies with the species and concentration of ions in the water, enabling the identification and quantification of heavy metal ions. By combining basic signal features with deep-learning-derived features, the IDMS achieves an average identification accuracy of 98% for six representative heavy-metal ions under practical conditions. In addition, coexisting-ion experiments were conducted to evaluate the applicability of the proposed framework under more realistic ionic backgrounds. Moreover, conditioned on the identified species, the device can quantify ion concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 500 μg/L with a detection limit of 0.1 μg/L, a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of less than 4%, and a response time of less than 80 ms. The IDMS also exhibits strong durability, maintaining stable performance over more than 500 testing cycles. Validation using river, lake, and tap water samples further demonstrates the performance of the IDMS in environmental water matrices, achieving an average classification accuracy of 91.2% and concentration prediction errors within 20%. The simple, low-cost, self-powered system provides a promising approach for on-site ion detection and water quality monitoring.

title: Modified fiber-coating composite tribovoltaic sensor for self-powered intelligent monitoring in spherical plain bearings
abstract: Spherical plain bearings are indispensable in high-end equipment, yet their intelligent advancement is hindered by the lack of reliable self-powered sensing technologies. Here, we report a robust fiber-coating composite tribovoltaic self-powered sensor (FC–TSPS), engineered via the formation of a Schottky junction between the graphene-modified liner (GM-L) and amorphous hydrogenated carbon (a-C:H) coating. The continuous conductive network formed through graphene doping transforms the conventional insulating composite liner, enabling efficient electron–hole pair separation and direct current generation at the friction interface. The sensing performance of the FC–TSPS was validated using a friction-testing platform, and its output mechanism was elucidated through energy-band diagram analysis. When integrated into spherical plain bearings, the FC–TSPS enables real-time monitoring of multidimensional motion states, including rotational frequency, load, and orientation, without compromising tribological performance of the bearings. Coupled with a deep-learning model, the system achieves highly accurate diagnosis (98.4%) across varying wear severities. Finally, the FC–TSPS exhibits exceptional reliability in an industrial hydraulic reciprocating machine, demonstrating a remarkable linear correlation (R2=0.9986) between signal frequency and actual rotational speed. This study provides a scalable technological paradigm for the intelligent evolution of core mechanical components and highlights significant potential for the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT).

title: Intelligent triboelectric sensor for rapid detecting of oil mixed in water
abstract: The frequent occurrence of water oil pollution poses a severe challenge to the security of global marine ecosystems and long-term human health. Here, an intelligent triboelectric oil-spill sensor (ITOS) with 8-electrode array, based on the dynamic contact-electrification at the liquid–solid interface, was developed for the rapid analysis of oil pollutants in water. When an oil-contained water droplet slides along an insulating solid surface, the triboelectric signals array along its trajectory can be recorded, enabling high performance analysis of the oil composition in water. By combining deep learning with ITOS, 16 types of oil pollutants were successfully identified with an ultrahigh detection accuracy exceeding 99.3% within 0.5 s. Additionally, the ITOS achieved an accuracy of 99.3% in distinguishing different oil concentrations and reached an ultralow classification-based detection limit of 10 ppb, enabling highly sensitive detection of trace oil contamination in water.

title: Bifurcation-gated kresling origami triboelectric mechanoreceptor enabling self-powered multimodal tactile sensing for intelligent human-robot interaction
abstract: Tactile sensors play major roles in human-robot interaction (HRI) by providing essential feedback on physical stimuli. In this context, bio-inspired design offers a promising route to reproducing the adaptive and multimodal sensing functions of biological tactile systems. Within this biomimetic framework, human-like tactile perception can be achieved by emulating the complementary dual-sensing behaviors of cutaneous mechanoreceptors, comprising Fast-Adaptive (FA) receptors responding to dynamic stimuli, and Slow-Adaptive (SA) receptors producing sustained responses to static stimuli. While triboelectric tactile sensors serve as substantial solutions, their sensing capability is primarily optimized for dynamic motion. In this study, we introduce a bifurcation-gated sensing strategy embodied in a Bio-inspired Origami-based Triboelectric mechanoreceptor (BOT) that discriminates between dynamic and static stimuli through a single compliant structure. The Kresling origami of the BOT exhibits a kinematic bifurcation at a buckling threshold. Below this threshold, dynamic loads produce FA mode, whereas static loads exceeding the threshold activate a SA mode that generates sustained signals during deformation. The BOT achieves highly linear sensing of indentation depth and normal force. Its practical utility is demonstrated through a self-powered collision detection system for safety and a deep learning-based material recognition framework capable of identifying properties under electromagnetic interference (EMI) environments. This work establishes the bifurcation-gated design principle as an alternative to multi-mechanism, opening a pathway toward triboelectric tactile sensors with mechanical property perception for HRI systems.

title: Janus triboelectric–LIG integrated smart mask for humidity-resistant dual-modal respiratory monitoring and intelligent analysis
abstract: Wearable respiratory monitoring systems capable of reliable operation under humid conditions are highly desirable for personalized healthcare, yet remain challenging due to moisture-induced signal instability and limited multimodal integration. Herein, we present an airflow–temperature dual-modal respiratory monitoring system (ATDM) integrated into a wearable mask for synchronized acquisition of respiratory airflow and thermal signals. The system integrates a Janus-structured triboelectric nanogenerator for airflow sensing and a flexible laser-induced graphene-based temperature sensor for thermal monitoring. The Janus structure effectively suppresses humidity-induced signal degradation, enabling stable operation even under high respiratory moisture conditions. Beyond sensing functionality, the device also exhibits efficient particulate filtration and antibacterial activity, ensuring practical wearing safety. By fusing airflow and temperature signals through a convolutional neural network model, the system achieves an overall classification accuracy of 99.17% for multiple respiratory states, including normal, slow, deep, fast breathing, and apnea. This work demonstrates a robust strategy for self-powered, humidity-resistant respiratory monitoring and highlights the potential of multimodal wearable systems for intelligent health management.

title: Real-CIF-guided generative discovery of MOF/PVDF-HFP solid-state electrolytes under coupled electrochemical–mechanical constraints
abstract: Solid-state electrolyte discovery requires route-specific design strategies that reconcile ion transport, electrochemical stability, interfacial compatibility, and mechanical integrity. In metal–organic framework (MOF)/polymer solid-state electrolytes, tunable pore apertures, metal nodes, and polar sites offer nanoscale control over ion transport and membrane reinforcement, yet framework-family selection remains largely empirical across the vast crystallographic space. Here, we establish MERITS, a data-driven generative discovery framework integrating transport-centered electrochemical learning, mechanics-aware constraints, bounded inverse generation, and real-CIF mining to identify experimentally actionable frameworks before synthesis. Within a PVDF-HFP-anchored design space, MERITS localizes a compact descriptor window and retrieves an isostructural Co/Mn-CPTC family for controlled validation. Co-CPTC@PVDF-HFP achieves a tensile strength of 42.59 MPa, an elongation at break of 726%, an ionic conductivity of 1.27 mS cm−1 at 25 °C, a Li+ transference number of 0.74, and an oxidative stability limit of 4.93 V. It further enables > 5000 h Li symmetric cycling, 1000-cycle LiFePO4 operation, 200-cycle NCM811 operation, and soft-package-cell validation. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics link this performance to a 6.8 Å aperture near the effective TFSI− size, preferential anion regulation, accessible Li+ migration, and framework-assisted stress transfer. This work establishes a real-structure-guided design-to-device route for reducing uncertainty in multiobjective MOF/polymer electrolyte discovery. Sensitivity calculations across 11 matrix profiles further show that the workflow can be re-applied beyond PVDF-HFP after re-localizing the matrix-specific descriptor window.

title: Generative inverse design of microsecond-response nanostructured heat flux sensors for hypersonic aerothermal environments
abstract: Accurate real-time measurement of transient heat flux is vital for the operational safety of hypersonic vehicles. However, conventional heat flux sensors suffer from millisecond-to-second response delays, static-only validation schemes, and empirically driven design strategies—critical limitations that severely hinder their applicability under extreme aerothermal conditions. Herein, we propose a generative inverse design framework integrating multi-physics simulation, data-driven optimization, MEMS fabrication, and hypersonic ground validation. A coupled thermal-mechanical-electrical model is established to quantify the influences of eight geometric parameters on the sensor’s response speed, detection sensitivity, and thermomechanical stress. A deep neural network surrogate model incorporated with a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model is trained on 147 finite-element simulation datasets for accurate sensor performance prediction. Targeting an ultrafast response of 50 μs, we generate one million nanostructured candidate designs and further screen them comprehensively in terms of thermal stress and sensitivity via the surrogate model, ultimately identifying an optimal configuration that concurrently achieves ultrafast response, superior high-temperature stability, and high sensitivity. The optimized nanostructured heat flux sensor, fabricated via standard MEMS processes, is validated through pulsed laser tests and plasma wind tunnel experiments. It delivers a 50 μs response time—two orders of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art sensors—while maintaining exceptional stability and structural integrity under extreme plasma aerothermal conditions. The proposed generative inverse design strategy substantially shortens the development cycle of nanostructured thermal sensors and offers a practical, reliable solution for real-time, precise heat flux measurement on hypersonic vehicles in harsh environments.

title: Flexible piezoelectric sensor array for intelligent monitoring system of body surface morphological abnormalities
abstract: Real-time dynamic monitoring of body-surface morphology is crucial for the early diagnosis of progressive diseases. However, the existing passive monitoring systems are unable to perceive the dynamic changes on the body surface and is even more difficult to achieve intelligent mapping of three-dimensional morphology. Here, we propose a novel intelligent monitoring system for abnormal human body-surface morphology based on dynamic curvature detection using a 2 × 8 flexible piezoelectric sensor array. By utilizing home-made multi-channel acquisition circuit and deep learning algorithms, the system maps deformation signals of the human skin surface collected by the array into a parametric human body model, enabling personalized real-time monitoring of normal morphology and posture. An abnormal deformation recognition module in the system is to accurately identify the location and degree of local abnormal shapes on the human body surface. Moreover, a morphological perception module in the system has been developed to integrate parametric human model mapping and abnormal deformation recognition functions, achieving 3D visualization of abnormal deformations and providing clinical diagnosis support. This work overcomes the limitations of traditional passive sensors that fail to recognize morphological information, offering technical support for the continuous monitoring of body surface morphology and the intelligent recognition of home environments.

title: A battery-free humidity sensor with machine-learning techniques
abstract:
Environmental and plant moisture levels are critical sensing parameters in various fields, including IoT-based crop irrigation, rare plant preservation, cultural heritage protection, meteorological monitoring, and marine engineering. However, existing humidity sensors face significant limitations, primarily due to power dependency, limited sensitivity, and a narrow measurement range. This study introduces a biomimetic bilayer structure composed of two polymers with distinct humidity responses, enabling the development of a self-powered humidity sensor. The sensor exhibits a rapid response time of 1.0 s and a recovery time of 0.6 s, effectively operating within a relative humidity (RH) range of 20–85%. At room temperature, the sensor demonstrates exceptional durability, maintaining stable performance without noticeable damage to the responsive layer even after over 200 full cycles. Integrating a machine learning-driven backend enhances the system's response speed and data accuracy. When connected to plant irrigation equipment, this system establishes a real-time adjustable humidity sensing mechanism. Upon detecting prolonged dryness in plant leaves, the irrigation equipment activates, while leaf humidity, environmental moisture levels, and irrigation volume data are simultaneously transmitted to the backend. This integration significantly elevates the intelligence and automation of plant irrigation. This research provides a rapid and real-time method for monitoring and adjusting humidity, offering technological support for advancements in smart cities, environmental monitoring, and plant conservation.

title: A wearable dual mode piezo-gel-MXene tactile synapse system enables AI diagnosis and staging of Parkinson’s disease
abstract:
Lack of objective, high-spatiotemporal-resolution tools to detect tremor dynamics and tactile dysfunction hampers early diagnosis and continuing monitoring of Parkinson’s disease (PD). We developed PGMAS, a bioinspired piezo‑gel–MXene artificial synapse that unifies mechanoreception and neuromorphic computation within a monolithic architecture, directly transducing normal and shear strain into spike‑like postsynaptic currents via mechano‑ionic coupling. PGMAS exhibits reflex‑like short‑term plasticity (∼100 ms), long‑term memory retention (>5000 s), and low‑pressure detectability (∼20 kPa), enabling in‑sensor analysis with minimal latency. To validate PGMAS, we performed clinical testing in PD, affixing fingertip sensors during standardized tasks (rest, arm elevation, grasping 500 g, grasping 1000 g) and natural object‑manipulation. Event‑resolved ΔPSC traces captured tremor frequency, amplitude and decay, differentiated stable grasp from intermittent and violent tremor, and revealed stage‑dependent phenotypes. A machine‑learning pipeline evaluated 60 task trials across four classes, achieving high diagnostic accuracy of 96.6%. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of real‑time, in‑sensor neuromorphic quantification of tremor in clinical settings and motivate larger, multi‑site and interventional studies to establish actionability, refine early‑stage discrimination, and define clinical benefit.

title: Machine-learning-optimized bioinspired metamaterials for broadband electromagnetic energy dissipation and wide-angle microwave absorption
abstract:
Achieving broadband absorption, wide-angle stability, polarization insensitivity, and low-profile thickness simultaneously remains a long-standing challenge for microwave-absorbing metamaterials. Although gradient-impedance structures can effectively suppress interfacial reflection, their absorption performance often deteriorates under oblique incidence and becomes polarization dependent, which limits practical deployment. Herein, inspired by the self-similar logarithmic spiral geometry of nautilus shells, we develop a bioinspired nonlinear honeycomb metamaterial absorber with logarithmic-spiral-derived inner walls. This nonlinear topology is integrated with magnetic-field-induced alignment of flaky carbonyl iron powder (FCIP), which constructs continuous magnetic-loss pathways within a silicone rubber matrix. A machine-learning-assisted inverse-design framework, combining random forest regression and a genetic algorithm, is further established to efficiently optimize the nonlinear impedance gradient. The fabricated absorber, with a thickness of 11.89 mm, achieves a measured effective absorption bandwidth (EAB), defined by reflection loss ≤ −10 dB, covering 4.08–18 GHz under TE polarization at an incidence angle of 40°. Stable absorption is also maintained under TE polarization from 0° to 40° and TM polarization from 0° to 60°. The synergistic coupling between the nonlinear impedance gradient and the oriented magnetic-particle network enables broadband electromagnetic energy dissipation over a wide angular range. This work provides a general strategy for the machine-learning-assisted nonlinear optimization of gradient-impedance absorbers.
